Supply chain, logistics, inventory & sales platform

Platform architecture & processes

What has been built so far: the system's structure, how a consignment moves from plan to reconciliation, how data flows, who uses what, and the data kept by each module. Version 1.1 · 18 October 2026 · source of truth: the code in this repository.

New in 1.1. Period plans are suggestions (Active / Replaced, no approval, no overlaps per company). Planners issue POs; director approval is a switch in apps/api/config.toml. Loading may differ from the PO within ±10% (or load alternatives), which creates a PO revision such as …-rev001. New Truck planner role. Office roles also get the team phone app (PWA) at /app/.

3apps on one server: office web, phone app (field roles + office team PWA), API
11roles, incl. truck planner; 3 field-only: loading point, driver, receiver
36database tables (PostgreSQL + PostGIS)
6integrations behind adapters: SMS/USSD, email, push, files, PDF, routing

1 · Architecture

One server, light apps, swappable integrations

diagrams/01-architecture.drawio

Clients. Office staff use the web app, or the team phone app (PWA) at /app/; the three field roles use the Android app, which queues work offline and sends it in one batch. Drivers without data can check in by SMS or USSD.

Server. One NestJS process serves the apps and the API at the same address. Every request passes auth, role and scope checks and is written to the audit log before a domain service runs the shared business rules. Business switches come from config.toml.

Data & integrations. PostgreSQL/PostGIS holds all operational data, including checkpoints and GPS. Each external service sits behind an adapter: without a key it uses a local stand-in, so nothing changes in code when keys are added.

1 · Architecture

Architecture explained

Layers

LayerWhat it isTechnology
Office web appPeriod plans, POs and revisions, loading queues, Truck desk, shipments, tracking map, stock, sales, finance, analytics, master data, users & devices.Svelte 5 + Vite · 112.7 KB first load · lazy map and charts
Field appMap-first, one action at a time: Hand over (from the PO, ±allowance meter, alternatives) · I've arrived / I'm leaving · Confirm receipt. Offline outbox, location, camera, push.Svelte 5 + Capacitor 7 (Android) · 73.5 KB
Team phone app (PWA)Office roles at /app/: bottom tabs per role, side drawer, home with menu, KPIs and “Needs attention”. Installable from the browser.apps/field/src/team
API gatewaySign-in (password or phone + PIN), rotating refresh tokens, remote device sign-out, role & scope guard (entity, loading point, warehouse), audit, idempotency keys, minimum app version.NestJS 11 on Fastify · JWT · bcrypt
Domain servicesPlanning & PO, logistics & tracking, stock, sales, finance, analytics, notifications, offline sync. All share one rules file with the web and field apps.TypeScript · packages/api/src/rules.ts
Data33 tables; nested items (plan lines, checkpoint passes, issues, acknowledgement lines) stored as JSON inside their parent record; GPS and geofences as PostGIS geography.PostgreSQL 17 + PostGIS 3.5 · Drizzle ORM
IntegrationsSMS/USSD (Africa's Talking), email (SMTP), push (Firebase), files (disk / S3), PDF letters (Typst), routing (OSRM). Each has a real adapter and a local stand-in.Adapters selected from .env
Business settingsPO approval on/off (default off), loading allowance ±10%, alternatives, revision suffix -rev. Sent to the apps in GET /v1/ref.apps/api/config.toml (or CONFIG_FILE)

Life of a request — a driver's check-in

  1. The driver slides I've arrived at Malaba; the app stores it in the outbox with a unique key and, when online, sends POST /v1/sync/batch.
  2. The gateway checks the token, role and that the leg belongs to this driver, audits the call, and the idempotency check applies a retried item once only.
  3. The tracking service records the pass (source: driver, geofence, SMS or office), recalculates leg status and ETA, and raises alerts.
  4. A result per item comes back; the app clears the outbox. Office screens see the change on their next refresh.

Running it

pnpm start starts the database and email inbox (Docker), migrates, seeds demo data if empty, builds both apps and serves everything from http://localhost:3101: / web, /app/ field, /brand/ logos, /v1 API.

Quality gates. pnpm verify (type-check, workflow test, API test, builds, size budget) · test:qa 638 API, security and integration checks (all passing) · pnpm e2e 95 browser steps across 7 user journeys.

2 · Process

From planning to reconciliation, by actor

diagrams/02-process.drawio

Read left to right. Each lane is a person or the system. Solid moving arrows are steps one person does in order; dotted orange moving arrows are hand-overs and notifications between people. Diamonds are decisions: the director's PO approval (dashed: only when purchase_orders = true; by default the planner's PO is issued at once) and the receiver's "final destination?" which either posts stock or starts a transfer leg. The truck planner lines up the queue and follows trucks and their costs.

4
2 · Process

Process steps and reconciliations

PhaseWhoWhat happensSystem record & control
1 Period planPlannerA suggestion per company and period. No approval; each save is a version. It gates nothing.Active / Replaced; no overlapping Active plans (409 → “Replace?”).
2 Purchase orderPlanner (→ Director if switched on)Planner fills truck lines and taps Issue purchase order. Letter on the company letterhead, emailed to the supplier.Ref per company and year (BTW-PO-2026-0002); “ISSUED” stamp, or director approval when purchase_orders = true.
3 Load & dispatchTruck planner · Loading pointTruck planner onboards providers and trucks and orders the queue. The loader loads from the PO within ±10%, may load alternatives, adds photo and agreed price, slides Hand over.Any difference → PO revision …-rev001 (auto-issued, notified); shipments follow the latest revision.
4 Route & monitorDriver · Truck planner · FleetDriver checks in at each checkpoint (slide, automatic geofence, or SMS/USSD), reports problems and "fixed".ETA early / on time / late; overdue and border-wait alerts.
5 ReceiveReceiver"Everything arrived OK", or adjust received / damaged per brand with photos; signs.Discrepancy alert; at a transfer point the next leg is planned.
6 Inventory & salesSystem · ReceiverStock posts only at the final warehouse after acknowledgement; sales reduce stock.Ledger per warehouse and SKU; sale above stock blocked unless a director overrides.
7 ReconcileAccounts · DirectorTransport payments and expenses recorded; dashboards show velocity flags and discrepancies.Payments above the threshold need director approval; landing cost per truck.

Reconciliations the platform performs

CheckRuleWhere it shows
Ordered vs loadedTruck total within ±allowance_pct of the PO and never above capacity; otherwise refused. A difference creates the next revision, numbered from the original PO; superseded orders are not counted twice.Allowance meter at hand-over, PO revision chain
Loaded vs received, per legEach leg: loaded − received = short; damaged counted separately; the next leg carries only good cases forward, so a loss is pinned to the leg where it happened.Shipment reconciliation table, discrepancy alert
Stock ledgerOpening + received + transfers in − transfers out − damaged ± adjustments − sold = closing; in-transit shown separately.Inventory (with ledger per SKU)
Transport feesAgreed price at loading vs payments made; balance and follow-up date per trip.Trip financials, balances by provider
Landing costGoods value + transport + taxes & duties + clearing + loading/offloading + storage = landing cost; ÷ cases = cost per case for stock value.Trip financials, inventory value
Offline replayEach phone action has one key; replays apply once and return the stored result.Sync screen, audit log

4 · Use cases

Who does what

diagrams/04-use-cases.drawio

Office roles (left) work in the web app or the team phone app (PWA). Field roles (right) use one task-focused screen each in the field app; drivers without data use SMS or USSD. Every action is limited to the person's scope: their entities, loading points or warehouses.
